Page title [07] Error Management, Anti-Loop & HITL (§15–16)
Section: Founder's POV Doc
Page [07] Error Management, Anti-Loop & HITL (§15–16) scope: MVP.
Page URL: https://ashishvats16.github.io/system-arch/page/founders-error-framework-hitl
Page [07] description: Marketplace error taxonomy.
Page [07] description: deterministic auto-fix loop.
Page [07] description: strict anti-loop retry rules.
Page [07] description: human-in-the-loop escalation boundaries.
15. Error Management Framework
Table header: Error Class | Example | Agent Behavior
Error class (§15 Error Management Framework): "Missing data".
Error class "Missing data" example: Fabric composition absent.
Agent behavior for "Missing data": Find source.
Agent behavior for "Missing data": if unavailable, ask seller.
Error class (§15 Error Management Framework): "Invalid value".
Error class "Invalid value" example: Marketplace does not accept seller's color term.
Agent behavior for "Invalid value": Map to allowed marketplace value.
Error class (§15 Error Management Framework): "Category mismatch".
Error class "Category mismatch" example: Product mapped to wrong product type.
Agent behavior for "Category mismatch": Reclassify.
Agent behavior for "Category mismatch": remap.
Error class (§15 Error Management Framework): "Variation error".
Error class "Variation error" example: Size/color relationship invalid.
Agent behavior for "Variation error": Rebuild mapping from canonical variant matrix.
Error class (§15 Error Management Framework): "Media error".
Error class "Media error" example: Image not accepted.
Agent behavior for "Media error": Identify failed image rule.
Agent behavior for "Media error": replace/remap if possible.
Error class (§15 Error Management Framework): "Content error".
Error class "Content error" example: Title/field violates marketplace rule.
Agent behavior for "Content error": Rewrite using verified facts.
Error class (§15 Error Management Framework): "Identifier error".
Error class "Identifier error" example: GTIN/identifier issue.
Agent behavior for "Identifier error": Ask seller.
Agent behavior for "Identifier error": use approved exemption flow if applicable.
Error class (§15 Error Management Framework): "Compliance error".
Error class "Compliance error" example: Required declaration missing.
Agent behavior for "Compliance error": Request exact compliance information.
Error class (§15 Error Management Framework): "Account permission".
Error class "Account permission" example: Seller not approved for category/brand.
Agent behavior for "Account permission": Create human action task.
Error class (§15 Error Management Framework): "Marketplace outage/technical".
Error class "Marketplace outage/technical" example: Submission unavailable.
Agent behavior for "Marketplace outage/technical": Retry according to safe retry policy.
Agent behavior for "Marketplace outage/technical": do not create duplicates.
Error class (§15 Error Management Framework): "Unknown error".
Error class "Unknown error" example: Unrecognized marketplace message.
Agent behavior for "Unknown error": Stop unsafe automation.
Agent behavior for "Unknown error": show raw message.
Agent behavior for "Unknown error": show plain-language summary (with the raw message).
Agent behavior for "Unknown error": create human task.
15.1 Error Resolution Loop
Error resolution loop step 27: Capture error exactly as returned.
Error resolution loop step 28: Normalize it into an internal error category.
Error resolution loop step 29: Identify affected field/variant/listing.
Error resolution loop step 30: Determine whether the error is deterministic and safely fixable.
Error resolution loop step 31: Apply fix if safe.
Error resolution loop step 32: Re-run validation.
Error resolution loop step 33: Resubmit.
Error resolution loop step 34: If still failing, stop repeated retries.
Error resolution loop step 34: If still failing, escalate.
Error resolution loop step 35: Show the seller the exact remaining action.
Important Anti-Loop Rule
The agent must never repeatedly submit the same failed listing indefinitely.
Every retry needs a changed input, a known retryable condition, or a marketplace status transition that justifies another attempt.
16. Human-in-the-Loop Rules
The product should be autonomous by default.
The product should not be reckless (autonomy by default, but not reckless).
Human involvement is a controlled exception.
Table header: Ask the Seller When | Do NOT Ask When
Ask the seller when: A critical factual field is genuinely missing.
Do NOT ask the seller when: The answer already exists in the canonical record.
Ask the seller when: Two authoritative sources conflict.
Do NOT ask the seller when: The value can be deterministically normalized.
Ask the seller when: Marketplace requires seller-specific approval/evidence.
Do NOT ask the seller when: The agent can safely transform an existing value.
Ask the seller when: A compliance declaration cannot be verified.
Do NOT ask the seller when: The missing value is merely a formatting variation.
Ask the seller when: A category/brand permission decision is required.
Do NOT ask the seller when: The marketplace has a known mapping for the category.

Section: Founder's POV Doc

Page URL: https://ashishvats16.github.io/system-arch/page/founders-quality-compliance-matrix
Page [08] description: Pre-submission quality gates (itemised in §17).

Page [08] description: marketplace requirement matrix (itemised in §19).
§17: quality gates are applied before submission.
Table header: Gate | Pass Condition
Quality gate "Identity" passes when: Brand, product type and seller SKU are coherent.
Quality gate "Classification" passes when: Marketplace category/product type selected with sufficient confidence.
Quality gate "Attributes" passes when: All required/conditional attributes are populated with valid values.
Quality gate "Variants" passes when: Every sellable variant has consistent identity.
Quality gate "Variants" passes when: Every sellable variant has consistent size/color.
Quality gate "Variants" passes when: Every sellable variant has required identifiers.
Quality gate "Media" passes when: Required media exists.
Quality gate "Media" passes when: Required media is associated correctly.
Quality gate "Content" passes when: Title/bullets/description/keywords are based on verified facts.
Quality gate "Content" passes when: Title/bullets/description/keywords are based on marketplace rules.
Quality gate "Compliance" passes when: Required product/packaging declarations are available where applicable.
Quality gate "Compliance" passes when: Seller information is available where applicable.
Quality gate "Commercial" passes when: MRP/price and other required commercial fields are internally consistent.
Quality gate "Submission" passes when: No known blocking validation issue remains.
18. Apparel Compliance Data to Capture
§18 is a business-data checklist, not legal advice.
The product should capture the compliance data listed in §18.
The product should avoid assuming legal compliance merely because fields are populated.
Table header: Compliance Data | Capture At | Notes
Compliance data "Manufacturer name/address" captured at: Brand + product.
Compliance data "Manufacturer name/address" note: Exact legal details where applicable.
Compliance data "Marketer/brand owner details" captured at: Brand/product.
Compliance data "Marketer/brand owner details" note: Where applicable.
Compliance data "Importer details" captured at: Product.
Compliance data "Importer details" note: For imported products where applicable.
Compliance data "Country of origin/manufacture" captured at: Product.
Compliance data "Country of origin/manufacture" note: Do not infer from brand location.
Compliance data "Consumer care contact" captured at: Brand.
Compliance data "Consumer care contact" note: Email/phone as applicable.
Compliance data "Size declaration" captured at: Variant/product.
Compliance data "Size declaration" note ("International size + metric measurements where required"): capture international size.
Compliance data "Size declaration" note ("International size + metric measurements where required"): capture metric measurements where required.
Compliance data "MRP inclusive of taxes" captured at: Variant/product.
Compliance data "MRP inclusive of taxes" note: Capture exact seller-declared MRP.
Compliance data "Fabric/fiber composition" captured at: Product.
Compliance data "Fabric/fiber composition" note: Capture exact composition rather than generic material wording.
Compliance data "Care instructions" captured at: Product.
Compliance data "Care instructions" note: Seller/manufacturer-provided.
Compliance data "Package declarations" captured at: Product/package.
Compliance data "Package declarations" note: Where applicable.
Compliance data "HSN/tax classification" captured at: Variant/product.
Compliance data "HSN/tax classification" note: Seller-provided/verified.
Compliance data "HSN/tax classification" note: do not blindly infer final tax classification.
Legal Metrology Garment Amendment (2022)
India's Department of Consumer Affairs has specific garment-related Legal Metrology requirements (2022 amendment).
2022 amendment: certain garment/hosiery sales require a declaration of manufacturer/marketer/brand owner/importer details.
2022 amendment: certain garment/hosiery sales require a declaration of consumer-care contact.
2022 amendment: certain garment/hosiery sales require a declaration of size.
2022 amendment: certain garment/hosiery sales require a declaration of MRP.
2022 amendment: the declared garment/hosiery information must be displayed on an e-commerce website.
General packaged-commodity rules also cover the declaration: manufacturer/packer/importer.
General packaged-commodity rules also cover the declaration: country of origin.
General packaged-commodity rules also cover the declaration: generic name.
General packaged-commodity rules also cover the declaration: net quantity.
General packaged-commodity rules also cover the declaration: MRP.
General packaged-commodity rules also cover the declaration: consumer care.

Page title [09] Master Field Dictionary & E2E Walkthrough (§20–21)
Section: Founder's POV Doc
Page [09] Master Field Dictionary & E2E Walkthrough (§20–21) scope: MVP.
Page URL: https://ashishvats16.github.io/system-arch/page/founders-master-field-dictionary
The master field dictionary is a complete 40+ column apparel dictionary.
The end-to-end walkthrough uses a real product: Women's Relaxed T-Shirt FSH-TEE-001.
§20 Master Field Dictionary defines the minimum V1 columns.
The §20 column set is the recommended spreadsheet-style column set for the initial apparel catalog intake.
The §20 column set can be presented to sellers as a simple template.
The dashboard can hide fields that are not relevant to the selected category.
